description: AstroHealth Command is a real-time health and life-support monitoring system for astronauts. It tracks vital signs (heart rate, SpO_2, body temperature) and suit conditions (CO_2, pressure, radiation) to detect medical risks instantly and guide autonomous emergency care during deep-space missions.
summary:
AstroHealth Command – An Intelligent Astronaut Health & Life-Support Monitoring System

AstroHealth Command, developed by Team Crew.Life, is a proposed real-time health and life-support monitoring software designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. The system brings important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen level (SpO₂), body temperature, blood sugar, sleep duration, and mood, into a single dashboard. It also monitors relevant spacecraft environmental and suit conditions, such as carbon dioxide levels, pressure, and radiation.

The software helps astronauts track their health, identify unusual changes, view trends, and receive clear alerts and guidance when readings require attention. It addresses the challenge by making health self-assessment easier and supporting early awareness of potential medical risks in isolated space environments.

AstroHealth Command is important because timely health monitoring can help astronauts make informed decisions, seek medical support when needed, and maintain their well-being during missions far from Earth.
details:
Project Details – AstroHealth Command

Team: Crew.Life

AstroHealth Command is a proposed astronaut health and life-support monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It aims to bring important health indicators and environmental information into one easy-to-understand dashboard.

What does it do and how does it work?

The proposed system monitors health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen level (SpO₂), body temperature, blood sugar, sleep duration and mood. It also considers environmental and life-support conditions such as carbon dioxide levels, pressure and radiation. The system is designed to display readings, track changes over time, identify unusual patterns and provide alerts or guidance when attention may be required.

What are its benefits?

It can help astronauts understand their health status, recognise changes earlier, maintain regular health check-ins and communicate concerns to medical support teams.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to support astronaut well-being and safer long-duration missions, especially when immediate medical assistance from Earth may not be available.

What makes the project creative?

The project combines personal health monitoring, spacecraft environmental awareness and understandable guidance in one proposed platform. It focuses on making complex health information easier for astronauts to review independently.

What factors did the team consider?

We considered the five major hazards of human spaceflight: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields and hostile closed environments. We also considered accessibility, simple visualisation, timely alerts, data reliability and the need for expert-validated medical guidance.

Tools and technologies

The current project showcase uses HTML and CSS, with a PowerPoint presentation and PDF demonstration. We have not yet developed a working monitoring application, live sensor integration or hardware prototype. No real astronaut health data is used; any sample readings are simulated.
